data.gender_notes: Bhoomitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhoomitha is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Bhu’ (earth) and ‘Mithra’ (goddess). The name signifies the goddess of the earth or the earth itself. It is a revered name in Hindu mythology, symbolizing stability, nourishment, and fertility. The name Bhoomitha carries the meaning “Earth Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhoomitha usually hope their child will grow to embody earth goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Bhoomitha evokes a sense of grounding and connection to the earth. Additionally, Bhoomitha is believed to be the embodiment of Shakti, the goddess of power and creation, further emphasizing her role as a creator, sustainer, and destroyer of all things. historical_references.reference: Bhoomitha Devi, also known as Prithvi Devi or Prithvi Goddess, is a Hindu goddess worshipped as the goddess of the earth. She is the wife of Vishnu in his Avatar as Vamana. The legend of Vamana is mentioned in the Mahabharata and Puranas. In this story, Vamana, disguised as a dwarf, asks King Mahabali for three paces of land. Mahabali, in his generosity, grants this wish. Vamana then grows to his true size and covers the three worlds. Bhoomitha Devi is the earth that Vamana steps on during this expansion.

Bhoomitha or Prithvi is also considered the primary wife of Rudra, the god of destruction, in the Shiva Purana. In this context, Prithvi is described as the earth, the goddess who forms the basis of all existence and sustains all living beings. She is said to have emerged from the navel of Brahma, the creator of the universe, and is often depicted as a throne for Shiva, symbolizing his connection to the earth and its manifestations.
